blocks.text: Here is how we prepare health and safety and environmental protection procedures step by step:

items: Analysis and identification: Risk analysis and hazard identification: The foundation is an assessment of workstations, technological processes and chemical substances in terms of risks to employees’ health and the environment, and identification of legal requirements.
Drafting the procedure: We write procedures clearly and, based on the risk analysis.
Consultation and implementation: Procedures should be discussed with employees and approved by senior management, and familiarising employees with the procedures through training.
Monitoring and updating: Regularly reviewing the effectiveness of procedures and updating them as processes change.

blocks.text: Here are the main objectives and benefits of creating health and safety procedures:
Health and safety procedures turn safety into a practical system, rather than just ‘red tape’. The main benefits are:

items: Protection and Standardisation: Risk minimisation and health protection – procedures enable the identification of hazards and specify how to proceed to avoid accidents. Standardisation of activities describes, step by step, how to perform tasks safely.

Legal requirement and avoidance of penalties: Employers are legally obliged to organise work in a way that ensures safe conditions. Implementing procedures protects against financial penalties during inspections.
Faster training and onboarding: Clear procedures help new employees learn safe working methods immediately. Increased work efficiency: A safe environment reduces sick leave and production downtime.
Proof of compliance: In the event of an accident, documented procedures serve as proof that the employer has done everything possible to ensure safety.

blocks.text: Structure of a procedure (what it should contain)
Each procedure should consist of the following elements:
Purpose and scope
Purpose of the procedure (what we aim to achieve) and scope of application (who and what the procedure applies to).
Responsibility
Who is responsible for implementation, supervision and compliance.
Procedure (step-by-step)
A detailed description of the actions, including emergencies (what to do if something goes wrong)
Documentation
Records, log sheets. Terminology: Explanation of difficult terms.
A detailed description of the actions, including emergencies (what to do if something goes wrong).
Organisational health and safety procedures
Health and Safety Procedures – Key Areas include, amongst others:

items: Health and safety management system: General principles and health and safety policy.
Health and safety training: Induction and periodic training (briefings).
Hazardous work: Procedures (e.g. work at height, hot work).
Personal protective equipment: Rules for allocation and use.

blocks.text: Environmental protection procedures
Pomagamy minimalizować wpływ firmy na otoczenie poprzez procedury:
Waste management
Sorting, storage and disposal of waste (including hazardous waste).
Emission control
Control of emissions from technological processes and control of wastewater and water consumption.
Procedures in the event of an environmental incident:
Spill or fire response plan.
Good practice

items: – Accessibility: Procedures must not simply be ‘documents gathering dust in a drawer’
– Involvement: We involve employees in drawing up procedures – they know the specifics of their work best.
– Visualisation: We encourage the use of graphical workstation instructions next to machinery.
